items.name: Partial derivative
items.formula: $\partial f/\partial x$: differentiate in $x$ with $y$ held fixed
items.when: To get the slope in one direction. On $x^2 + 2y^2$ the two are $2x$ and $4y$.

items.name: Gradient
items.when: It points the way $f$ rises fastest, so $-\nabla f$ is the way down.

items.name: Bottom of a bowl
items.when: To find a minimum by algebra: set every partial derivative to 0 and solve.

items.name: Gradient descent step
items.when: Every step, with the gradient at the point you are at now. Subtract; never add.

items.name: Check the step
items.when: After every step. If $f$ went up, $\eta$ is too big or the sign is wrong.

items.name: Factor per step
items.when: To predict a run of steps in one direction: negative factor bounces, size above 1 blows up.

items.name: When it converges
items.when: To choose $\eta$: the largest eigenvalue (the steepest direction) sets the limit for every direction.

items.name: How f shrinks
items.when: To see that $f$ falls every step even while $x$ bounces, as long as $|1 - \eta\lambda| < 1$.

items.name: Gradient of a bowl
items.when: For any bowl given by a symmetric $H$. Its eigenvectors are the steep and shallow directions.

items.name: Condition number
items.when: To predict how slow descent will be. Large $\kappa$ means a narrow valley and a zig-zag.

items.name: Best single step
items.when: When one fixed $\eta$ must serve both directions: both factors then have the same size.

items.name: Least-squares gradient
items.when: To train a least-squares fit. $A^\mathsf{T}(b - Ax)$ is minus this: it points uphill.

items.name: Where the walk stops
items.when: Zero gradient is the normal equations: walking down and solving reach the same point.
